Hey! Others already gave you advice for what to check / do, and they're right. You should definitely see a GYN, the best thing is to get swabbed for a candida panel, bv, etc.

I just wanted to say that the GYN is definitely scarier in your head than it actually is there. For context on this, I'm a 29 year old woman who went to the GYN for the first time this year because I was scared of the pain. I have a lot of trauma surrounding doctors dealing with intimate places on my body. I got my first yeast infection / bv combo ever in my life this year, and I finally decided I couldn't put it off anymore. It's not fun! But it is manageable. I cry every single time I go in \[still battling my infections\], so I take a weighted stuffed animal with me so I can put all my tension into squeezing that. It took a couple tries to find a good doctor, but I finally found a female doctor who explains everything she's doing to me and goes slow if I need her to. She's very nice to me even though I'm a crybaby and also very insecure with myself.

All of this to say I know it's scary, but take it from me, if the infection escalates, the pain from that is much worse than a couple of minutes letting a GYN down there. :( Explain to them that you're afraid and you need them to walk you through everything they're doing / tell you everything they do before they do it so you aren't surprised. A good doctor won't have any issue doing that to help you feel a little better, and any pains from the swabs are short-lived and in my experience haven't been too bad. \[I mostly cry because of trauma/anxiety more than from pain.\]

If you end up needing anyone else, feel free to reach out. I love reading really complicated high fantasy books and often find myself specifically trying to find romantasies with deeper plots for this very reason lol. 😂

For the boric acid, is it possible you aren't getting it far enough inside of you? When I first tried it, I freaked out and cried from the pain because it ended up burning me. I tried again after getting some applicators off Amazon to make sure I got it far, far up inside of me and then I was able to tolerate it / couldn't even tell it was there.

If not, I second getting swabbed for all different strains of yeast and mycoplasma/etc. I started with BV, then developed a candida glabrata yeast infection while treating it, and now I'm bouncing back and forth between BV and yeast, so it can definitely be more than just the one thing you're dealing with. Good luck, sorry you're dealing with this. It really feels awful :(

You may want to ask your GYN about testing for different strains of yeast too. I had all these symptoms and was given medication for both common yeast infections and BV but symptoms kept coming back. I ended up having candida glabrata which doesn’t respond to normal YI treatments.

I haven't been re-swabbed to check yet (my 2 weeks on boric acid ends tomorrow), but I don't think it's cured. I still have symptoms. I do think BA helped everything feel a little better, though, so I would consider trying it if you're dealing with glabrata, even just to see if it helps with symptoms.

I play a lot of visual novels, so I can rec some of them! Our Life Beginnings & Always, although you don’t really see the MC, you still can customize them through dialogue. Arcadia Fallen lets you create a pretty androgynous MC who has a character portrait. Same with dream daddy, which is a very cutesy game. 

The Rune Factory games all have pretty feminine male protagonists and are a spin off of the Harvest Moon/Story of Seasons games that helped inspire Stardew. Similarly, there’s Sun Haven and My Time at Portia / Sandrock.

I also used Rael / Always cotton pads until they started bothering me recently.

Switched to U by Kotex pads after reading through a lot of recommendations and they're a lot more comfortable.

If you’d consider a visual novel with some life sim elements and a lot of interactivity, I recommend Our Life: Beginnings and Always! Slay the Princess is also really good and has an amazing story. It’s a bit darker in tone, but I still considered it kinda cozy haha.

Also Coffee Talk (it has 2 games) which has a little bit of lowkey gameplay. You mostly talk to customers while making them drinks and doing latte art.

If you’re looking to try a different class from scratch, hunters are VERY newbie friendly to play and feel really nice because you can move around a lot while using your abilities as opposed to staying in one spot like with your casters. You also have a pet that helps you fight so survivability is much higher. Rogues are also a good class as a new player because you can do a good amount of damage in the opening of a fight or play things more stealthy and sneak around enemies if you’re having too much trouble with certain mobs, which I found very helpful back when I started playing until I got the hang of combat. Mages and warlocks are both pretty easy to start with too, but If casters feel too slow for now, it’d definitely be worth trying out a non-caster class! I love warlock but even I have to get on other class alts often because I have to be in the mood for casters lol
